observation.visible_scene: Corner of a room with off-white walls, a window on the right showing trees, a white folding table on the left holding rows of colorful building blocks, and a neon sign reading 'DESIGN BUILD PEOPLE!' partly visible on the left wall. The wooden floor is covered with large interlocking toy blocks arranged into structures: a tall white arched tower at the back-left, a dark-blue wall and a yellow hollow cube beside it, a blue hollow cube and an orange cluster in the center, a white hollow cube and a tall stepped blue tower on the right, plus a central heap of loose multicolored blocks. In the foreground are flat mats of orange, magenta and red blocks with black borders, scattered loose pieces, and a product box.
visible_changes: The tall white arched tower at the back-left steadily loses height across the excerpt, slumping from a clear arch into a low mound against the wall.
The tall stepped blue tower on the right likewise collapses progressively, shrinking from a multi-level column to a short heap.

The central heap of loose blocks spreads and flattens: the dark-blue vertical cluster seen early on disperses into the broader multicolored pile, and the white/yellow/orange pieces in the center fan outward.

The standing structures that remain (dark-blue wall, yellow hollow cube, blue hollow cube, orange base, white hollow cube, foreground mats, table blocks, box) stay largely in place with only minor surface shifts.
No camera pan or zoom is evident; the table, window, neon sign and floor edges hold the same framing throughout, so the changes are object motion, not viewpoint motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the collapse of the two towers (no operator or impact is visible in this excerpt).
Whether the footage is sped-up/time-lapse or real-time.
The final resting state of the towers and the central pile after the last frame.
The original full heights of the towers before the excerpt began.
uncertain_details: Exact per-frame heights of the collapsing towers are hard to measure due to block clutter and lighting.
Small deformations of the yellow and blue hollow cubes are ambiguous and may be occlusion rather than movement.
It is unclear whether the central spreading is a true collapse of a structure or just rearrangement of an already-loose pile.
